findings.title: LLM client has no request timeout or retry — refine supervisor call can hang a worker thread indefinitely
findings.whatExists: llm.py builds ChatOpenAI/ChatAnthropic clients. The search tools (flights/hotels/tickets) bound their provider calls with query_parallel(timeout=20/25). main.py bounds full plans with a semaphore + PLAN_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT and runs them via asyncio.to_thread.
findings.whatsMissing: get_llm() constructs the chat models with only model/temperature/max_tokens/base_url — no `timeout`/`request_timeout` and no `max_retries` (llm.py:80-89 for OpenAI, 105-114 for Anthropic). The agent LLM calls (itinerary/tour structured_output.invoke) and especially refine.py's supervisor.invoke (refine.py:772) are NOT wrapped by query_parallel's wall-clock timeout. refine_plan's create_react_agent + supervisor.invoke has no internal timeout; if the provider stalls, the call blocks the asyncio.to_thread worker for as long as the underlying HTTP client's default allows (langchain/httpx defaults can be very long or effectively unbounded behind a proxy). With MAX_CONCURRENT_PLANS workers, a few stalled LLM calls can exhaust the pool. _handle_chat catches exceptions but cannot interrupt a blocked synchronous call.
findings.evidence: backend/llm.py:80-89 and backend/llm.py:105-114 (kwargs build with no timeout/max_retries); backend/refine.py:772 (`result = supervisor.invoke({...})` with no timeout); agents/itinerary.py:133 and agents/tour.py:112 (structured.invoke with no timeout).
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit `timeout=` (e.g. 30-60s) and `max_retries=` to both ChatOpenAI and ChatAnthropic in llm.py, and/or run supervisor.invoke under a hard deadline (e.g. asyncio.wait_for around the to_thread, or a concurrent.futures timeout). This bounds tail latency and prevents worker-pool exhaustion under provider degradation.

findings.title: CI runs backend tests without a database or alembic upgrade, and has no migration/model-drift check
findings.whatExists: There is exactly one Alembic migration (36ee394e0625_init_enterprise_floor.py) and it matches models.py (user_profiles, saved_trips with the composite index, saved_constraints). railway.json runs `alembic upgrade head` in the deploy start command. db.py falls back to a SQLite file locally and tests use rebind_for_tests + Base.metadata.create_all.
findings.whatsMissing: The CI backend job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:60-86) installs deps, byte-compiles, and runs `python -m unittest discover -s tests` with NO Postgres service container and NO `alembic upgrade head` step. So migrations are never executed in CI against a real Postgres — a broken migration (bad SQL, JSONB/UUID dialect issue, or missing migration after a model change) would not be caught until a live Railway deploy. There is also no autogenerate-drift guard (e.g. `alembic check` / `alembic revision --autogenerate` diff), even though the enterprise-floor plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-27-enterprise-floor.md:53) explicitly called for CI to 'add db service, alembic check'. Because nothing in app boot calls create_all/upgrade, a future model edit without a matching migration would pass all 131 unit tests (they create_all from current models) yet break production where only migrations run.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:60-86 (backend job: no services:, no alembic step); railway.json:8 (only place alembic upgrade runs — at deploy time); docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-27-enterprise-floor.md:53 ('ci.yml MODIFY (add db service, alembic check ...)') vs actual ci.yml which has neither; tests create schema via Base.metadata.create_all (tests/test_repository.py:30, tests/test_main_trip_ws.py:29) not via migrations.
findings.recommendation: Add a Postgres `services:` block to the CI backend (or a dedicated migration) job and run `alembic upgrade head` against it, plus an `alembic check` (or autogenerate-diff that fails on non-empty output) so model/migration drift and broken migrations are caught before deploy rather than on the live database.

findings.title: No React error boundary — Sentry is initialized but never used to catch render errors; any component throw blanks the entire app
findings.whatExists: Sentry.init() runs at startup in src/main.jsx:11-17 when VITE_SENTRY_DSN_FRONTEND is set. @sentry/react is a dependency (package.json:18).
findings.whatsMissing: No <ErrorBoundary> wraps the app (neither Sentry.ErrorBoundary nor a custom one), and no componentDidCatch/getDerivedStateFromError exists anywhere. The only Sentry reference in the whole codebase is the init call. Because React 19 unmounts the entire tree on an uncaught render error, any throw inside App/ResultCard/BudgetPanel/transformResults etc. produces a permanently blank black screen (body background #0a0a0a) with no fallback UI and no error reported to Sentry from the render path.
findings.evidence: grep for ErrorBoundary|componentDidCatch|getDerivedStateFromError|Sentry\. across frontend returns only src/main.jsx:12 (Sentry.init). frontend/src/main.jsx:19-29 renders <App/> (optionally wrapped in ClerkProvider/AuthGate) with no error boundary. @sentry/react imported at frontend/src/main.jsx:4 but Sentry.ErrorBoundary never used.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the rendered tree in Sentry.ErrorBoundary (from @sentry/react) with a fallback UI (e.g. a 'Something went wrong — Reload' card), or a custom class ErrorBoundary when Sentry DSN is unset. This both prevents the blank-screen failure and ensures render errors reach Sentry.

findings.title: Stuck 'GO' spinner: a WebSocket close/error during chat (phase 'done') never resets chatLoading
findings.whatExists: On the normal chat path the backend sends reply->result->done and the 'done' handler resets chatLoading (prototype.jsx:210-214); the 'error' handler also resets it (prototype.jsx:215-219).
findings.whatsMissing: chatLoading is set true in handleChat (prototype.jsx:392) but the ws onerror handler (prototype.jsx:277-281) only does setPhase(running?done) + setSpeaking(false) and does NOT reset chatLoading. The ws onclose handler (prototype.jsx:282-297) only resets chatLoading inside the prev==='running' branch. During a chat refinement the phase is already 'done', so if the socket errors/closes after the user hits GO but before reply/done arrives, chatLoading stays true forever: the input stays disabled and the GO button is stuck showing '...' with no way to recover except RESET.
findings.evidence: frontend/prototype.jsx:384-396 handleChat sets setChatLoading(true) with no timeout. onerror frontend/prototype.jsx:277-281 omits setChatLoading(false). onclose frontend/prototype.jsx:289-296 calls setChatLoading(false) ONLY when prev==='running'; chat runs while phase==='done'. ChatInput disables input/button on chatLoading (frontend/components/ChatPanel.jsx:19,22).
findings.recommendation: Always setChatLoading(false) in both ws.onerror and ws.onclose handlers (unconditionally, not just in the running branch), and/or add a watchdog timeout that clears chatLoading after N seconds with an error message.

findings.title: Calendar fetch failure has no distinct error/empty/retry UI — grid is stuck on 'Loading... (is backend running?)' indefinitely
findings.whatExists: The calendar fetch (prototype.jsx:109-137) logs failures to the debug trace (calendar.fetch.error) and guards against non-array bodies. GpSelect shows a placeholder when gpList is empty (GpSelect.jsx:45-49).
findings.whatsMissing: There is exactly one state for both 'still loading' and 'fetch failed': the empty-list branch renders the static string 'Loading calendar... (is backend running?)'. On HTTP error, network error, or non-array body, gpList stays [] and the user sees the same perpetual 'Loading' message with no error styling, no retry button, and no distinction between in-progress and failed. There is no loading skeleton/spinner either; debugMode is required to even see the error reason in the trace.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/GpSelect.jsx:45-49 single empty-state branch text 'Loading calendar... (is backend running?)'. frontend/prototype.jsx:118-134 error paths only call pushDebug and return; no error state is surfaced to GpSelect (no prop for fetch status/error). No retry control anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Track calendar fetch status (loading|error|empty|ready) in App and pass it to GpSelect; render a real error state with a Retry button on failure and a spinner/skeleton while loading.

findings.title: No global unhandledrejection / window.onerror handler — async failures outside try/catch are silently dropped
findings.whatExists: Most async paths have local try/catch (calendar fetch, clipboard copy, JSON.parse in handlers). Sentry, when DSN is set, captures via its default integrations.
findings.whatsMissing: There is no window 'unhandledrejection' or 'error' listener registered by the app (grep returns none). When Sentry DSN is unset (the documented local/prod-without-Sentry fallback per the enterprise-floor description), unhandled rejections (e.g. a throw inside an awaited buildWsUrl/getToken not wrapped, or future async additions) vanish with no user-facing feedback and no logging beyond the browser console. handleWsMsg's JSON.parse (prototype.jsx:150) is not wrapped in try/catch, so a malformed frame throws inside the ws onmessage callback as an uncaught error.
findings.evidence: grep for unhandledrejection|window.onerror|addEventListener('error' across frontend returns none. frontend/prototype.jsx:149-150 handleWsMsg does JSON.parse(evt.data) with no try/catch (contrast SavedTrips.jsx:17-21 which wraps its parse). Sentry is conditional on DSN (src/main.jsx:11).
findings.recommendation: Register window 'unhandledrejection' and 'error' listeners (report to Sentry when available, otherwise console.error + optional toast), and wrap the JSON.parse in handleWsMsg in try/catch like SavedTrips already does.

findings.title: Accessibility gaps on primary interactive elements: clickable <div> cards/rows lack role/keyboard, buttons lack type, modals lack focus trap
findings.whatExists: Good spots exist: ExplainabilityPanel has role='dialog', aria-label, Escape-to-close (ExplainabilityPanel.jsx:7-11,25,37), and explain buttons carry aria-label (ResultCard.jsx:68). WelcomeForm inputs have associated <label> text. index.html sets lang='en' (index.html:2) and a viewport meta.
findings.whatsMissing: (a) GP cards are plain <div onClick> with no role='button', tabIndex, or onKeyDown — keyboard users cannot select a Grand Prix (GpSelect.jsx:23-37). (b) Result rows are clickable <div onClick> with no role/keyboard (ResultCard.jsx:48). (c) Many <button>s omit type (default 'submit') — harmless today since there's no <form>, but a latent bug (e.g. WelcomeForm currency/stand/submit buttons, ChatPanel, AppChrome). (d) The Explainability and SavedTrips slide-over modals do not trap focus or move focus to the panel on open / restore it on close (ExplainabilityPanel.jsx, SavedTrips.jsx:79). (e) WelcomeForm labels are visually associated by proximity but not programmatically linked via htmlFor/id, so screen readers may not pair them (WelcomeForm.jsx:25-27).
findings.evidence: frontend/components/GpSelect.jsx:23-37 (div onClick, no role/tabIndex/onKeyDown). frontend/components/ResultCard.jsx:48 (div onClick toggle, no keyboard). frontend/components/WelcomeForm.jsx:25-40 (<label> + <input> with no htmlFor/id pairing). No focus-trap/initial-focus logic in ExplainabilityPanel.jsx or SavedTrips.jsx. Buttons across components omit type= attribute.
findings.recommendation: Make GP cards and result rows keyboard-operable (role='button', tabIndex=0, onKeyDown for Enter/Space), add type='button' to all non-submit buttons, link form labels via htmlFor/id, and add focus management (move focus in on open, restore on close, trap Tab) to both slide-over panels.

findings.title: Frontend has zero static-analysis gate (no lint, no typecheck, no TypeScript) — UX/dead-code regressions go uncaught

The code even relies on eslint-disable comments (prototype.jsx:41) for a real Rules-of-Hooks edge, but no ESLint actually runs to enforce hooks rules, unused imports, undefined vars, or a11y (eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y). Ground-truth frontend step 5 (passed:false): 'No eslint config, no tsconfig, no prettier config, and no .ts/.tsx files anywhere'. eslint-disable comment present at frontend/prototype.jsx:41 with no ESLint to honor it.

findings.title: Saved-trips load relies on a fire-and-forget WS message with no per-card loading/error feedback; load failures are partially silent

The SAVE button shows 'SAVED' only on save_trip_ack (prototype.jsx:220-223) but has no error/failure state if no ack arrives (e.g. ws drops) — it silently stays 'SAVE'. window.confirm for delete is also a blocking native dialog rather than an in-app confirm (minor UX inconsistency).

findings.title: No lint, type-check, or coverage gate in CI or local scripts (backend or frontend)
findings.whatExists: ci.yml runs backend byte-compile + unittest + skill tests, frontend build + npm audit, full Playwright lane, bundled check-local.sh, gitleaks, agent-doc-sync. check-local.sh mirrors the same compile/test/build/audit steps.

No test coverage measurement (no pytest-cov, no coverage in requirements.txt or CI). frontend package.json has only dev/build/preview/e2e scripts — no lint/typecheck. The codebase is plain JS/JSX with no TypeScript, so there is no type safety at all on the frontend.

Mirror them in check-local.sh so the local gate and CI stay equivalent. Even a non-blocking eslint pass would catch the kind of dead-import/undefined-var bugs that JS/JSX silently ships.

findings.title: Flagship enterprise feature E2E (saved_trips Postgres round-trip) never runs in CI
findings.whatExists: frontend/e2e/saved_trips.spec.js exists and exercises the save/load round-trip (the headline enterprise-floor feature). playwright.config.js gates it behind E2E_INCLUDE_SAVED=1.
findings.whatsMissing: The CI e2e job sets only E2E_INCLUDE_REFINE=1 LLM_STUB_MODE=1 — it never sets E2E_INCLUDE_SAVED=1, so saved_trips.spec.js is silently excluded from every CI run. The single most important enterprise-floor capability (Postgres-backed saved trips, which the deploy runbook step 6.3 manually verifies) has no automated regression coverage in the pipeline.

findings.recommendation: Add E2E_INCLUDE_SAVED=1 to the CI e2e lane (the spec already runs against the SQLite local fallback, so no Postgres service is needed). If it requires a DB service, add a Postgres service container to the e2e job and run the saved-trips spec there.

findings.title: No Python runtime version pin for Railway/NIXPACKS; CI, local venv, and prod can diverge
findings.whatExists: railway.json uses NIXPACKS builder with buildCommand `pip install -r requirements.txt`. CI pins python-version '3.12'. Local venv is python3.11.
findings.whatsMissing: No runtime.txt, .python-version, nixpacks.toml, or pyproject [requires-python] anywhere in the repo, so Railway's NIXPACKS picks its own default Python at build time. Production therefore runs an unpinned, possibly different interpreter than both CI (3.12) and local (3.11). For a stack with psycopg3 binary wheels, alembic, and pydantic, a silent major-version drift can change behavior or break wheels.
findings.evidence: railway.json:3-5 (builder NIXPACKS, no python pin); find for backend/runtime.txt, runtime.txt, backend/.python-version, .python-version, backend/pyproject.toml all MISSING; ci.yml:72 pins '3.12'; ground-truth backend step 1 shows local venv -> python3.11.
findings.recommendation: Add a runtime pin Railway honors (e.g. nixpacks.toml `[phases.setup] nixPkgs = ['python311']` or a `.python-version`/`runtime.txt`) matching the CI Python (3.12) so all three environments agree. Align CI to the same version too.

findings.title: Database migration rollback (alembic downgrade) is undocumented; runbook 'rollback' only reverts code, not schema
findings.whatExists: README section 7 and docs/deployment-design.md sections 10/11.6 document a rollback drill via platform per-revision rollback + re-running deploy-smoke. The init migration has a working downgrade() (backend/alembic/versions/36ee394e0625_init_enterprise_floor.py:63-72).
findings.whatsMissing: Neither the runbook nor deployment-design mentions `alembic downgrade` or what to do when a deploy that included a schema migration is rolled back. Railway per-revision rollback reverts the *code* to a prior revision, but the schema migration already applied at deploy time (`alembic upgrade head` in railway.json:8) is NOT undone. If a future migration is destructive or backward-incompatible, code-rollback alone leaves old code running against a newer schema — a data/availability hazard with no documented procedure.
findings.evidence: grep for 'alembic downgrade|downgrade head|schema rollback' across docs/deployment-design.md and README.md returns nothing; README.md:557-559 (rollback = dashboard per-revision only); railway.json:8 (migrations applied at every deploy start); deployment-design.md:476-482 rollback section covers only platform revision + log/cache notes.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Migration rollback' subsection to the runbook: when a rolled-back deploy crossed a migration boundary, document running `cd backend && alembic downgrade -1` (or to a named revision) against the live DB, and state the policy that migrations must stay backward-compatible across one deploy (expand-contract) so code-only rollback is always safe.

findings.title: deploy-smoke workflow is manual-only and disconnected from the deploy pipeline
findings.whatExists: deploy-smoke.yml verifies /healthz, /readyz (DB up), /api/calendar 401-gating, optional demo-token path, frontend HTML load, and a frontend-bundle secret-leak scan. README step 6 instructs running it after each deploy.
findings.whatsMissing: The workflow only has a workflow_dispatch trigger (manual, requires hand-typing backend_url/frontend_url each time). It is not invoked on deploy, not scheduled, and not chained from CI. A bad production deploy (DB down, auth misconfigured, secret leak) is therefore only caught if a human remembers to run it. There is no automated post-deploy gate despite the project framing 'deploy-gate verification' as the T-DEPLOY-VERIFY deliverable.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-smoke.yml:11 (only `workflow_dispatch:`, no schedule/push/repository_dispatch); no deploy job in ci.yml references it (ci.yml has no deploy/smoke chaining); README.md:549 (manual 'Run workflow').
findings.recommendation: Add a `schedule` (e.g. daily cron) trigger with the prod URLs hardcoded or read from repo variables, and/or a `repository_dispatch`/`workflow_run` trigger so the smoke runs automatically after a deploy. At minimum store backend_url/frontend_url as repo variables so the manual run is one click.

findings.title: Documented-but-unused env vars in backend/.env.example (REQUIRE_DEMO_TOKEN, CLERK_SECRET_KEY, FLIGGY_*, BOCHA_API_KEY)
findings.whatExists: backend/.env.example documents these as configurable.
findings.whatsMissing: None of them is read by any non-test project code. REQUIRE_DEMO_TOKEN (.env.example:52) is explicitly dead — main.py:87 comment says the old _REQUIRE_DEMO_TOKEN was removed as never-read dead code. CLERK_SECRET_KEY (.env.example:73 AND README:524 prod instructions) is never referenced — backend Clerk auth is pure JWKS verification (CLERK_JWT_ISSUER + CLERK_JWKS_URL only), so operators are told to set an unused secret in production. FLIGGY_APP_KEY/FLIGGY_APP_SECRET/BOCHA_API_KEY (.env.example:59-61) have no reader anywhere.
findings.evidence: grep REQUIRE_DEMO_TOKEN backend (non-venv,non-test) -> only main.py:87 dead-code comment; grep CLERK_SECRET_KEY backend (non-venv) -> exit 1 (no matches) while .env.example:73 and README.md:524 list it; grep FLIGGY|BOCHA backend (non-venv) -> exit 1, only present at .env.example:59-61.
findings.recommendation: Remove REQUIRE_DEMO_TOKEN, FLIGGY_*, and BOCHA_* from .env.example (or implement them). For CLERK_SECRET_KEY, drop it from both .env.example:73 and README:524 prod instructions, or add a code comment that it is reserved/unused so operators don't provision an unnecessary secret.

findings.title: Used-but-undocumented env vars (ENV, LOG_LEVEL, LLM_STUB_MODE)
findings.whatExists: These vars are read at runtime but absent from backend/.env.example.
findings.whatsMissing: ENV is read as a fallback for APP_ENV (auth.py:50, main.py:81) but never documented — an operator who sets ENV=production expecting it to enable prod gating would be relying on undocumented behavior. LOG_LEVEL controls logging verbosity (logging_config.py:55) and is undocumented. LLM_STUB_MODE (refine.py:724, agents/tickets.py:43, agents/transport.py:57) is a test/CI determinism switch with no .env.example mention, so its production-safety implications are undocumented.
findings.evidence: auth.py:50 (`os.environ.get("APP_ENV") or os.environ.get("ENV")`), main.py:81 (same); logging_config.py:55 (`os.environ.get("LOG_LEVEL", "INFO")`); refine.py:724 + agents/tickets.py:43 + agents/transport.py:57 read LLM_STUB_MODE; none of ENV/LOG_LEVEL/LLM_STUB_MODE appear in backend/.env.example (grep confirmed).
findings.recommendation: Document LOG_LEVEL (with default INFO) and the ENV alias in .env.example. Document LLM_STUB_MODE in the testing/E2E section noting it must never be set in production (it forces deterministic mock LLM output).

findings.title: Required production config (Clerk issuer, OPENAI_API_KEY) has only request-time guards, not a startup fail-fast
findings.whatExists: main.py lifespan fails fast if ALLOWED_ORIGINS is empty in a non-local env (main.py:194-198). auth.py returns HTTP 503 at request time if CLERK_JWT_ISSUER is unset while in prod/require-clerk mode (auth.py:196-200, 253-254). llm.py logs and falls back to mock if OPENAI/ANTHROPIC keys are missing (llm.py:71-72, 96-97).
findings.whatsMissing: Only ALLOWED_ORIGINS is guarded at boot. A production deploy with REQUIRE_CLERK_AUTH=true (or APP_ENV=production) but a missing/typo'd CLERK_JWT_ISSUER boots cleanly and passes /healthz (and even /readyz if DB is up), then 503s on every authenticated request — green probe, dead app. Likewise a prod deploy missing OPENAI_API_KEY boots green and silently serves mock itineraries instead of failing or warning loudly. There is no startup assertion that the auth/LLM config required by the active APP_ENV is actually present.
findings.evidence: main.py:194-198 guards only ALLOWED_ORIGINS in lifespan; auth.py:196-200 (503 'CLERK_JWT_ISSUER required in production' is request-time, inside require_user, not startup); llm.py:71-72 (`if not os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"): logger.info(... mock fallback)`); health.py:24-26 /healthz returns 200 unconditionally regardless of auth/LLM config.
findings.recommendation: Extend the lifespan startup guard: when not local, also require CLERK_JWT_ISSUER (and JWKS URL) whenever Clerk auth is enforced, and require the LLM key for the selected LLM_PROVIDER (or at least emit a WARNING-level startup log when prod is running on mock LLM). Fail fast so the platform healthcheck reflects a genuinely-misconfigured deploy instead of reporting green.

findings.title: CI does not run the secret-scan or agent-doc-sync inside the local gate, and the local gate omits them — partial CI/local contract mismatch
findings.whatExists: CI has dedicated gitleaks and agent-docs jobs (ci.yml:38-58) plus a bundled-check-local job that runs scripts/check-local.sh (ci.yml:170-201). The .githooks/pre-push runs check-agent-doc-sync.sh + check-local.sh.
findings.whatsMissing: scripts/check-local.sh (the script contributors are told to trust) does NOT include a secret scan (gitleaks) at all, so a developer running only the local gate gets no secret-leak signal that CI enforces. The local gate and CI are therefore not equivalent for the security-relevant gitleaks check — a contributor can pass the full local gate and still be blocked by CI on secrets. The README/deployment-design frame check-local.sh as the trustworthy local mirror of CI.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-local.sh:14-34 (steps 1-7: agent-sync, compile, unit tests, skill tests, frontend install/build/audit — no gitleaks); ci.yml:47-58 gitleaks job exists only in CI; .githooks/pre-push runs check-local.sh but not gitleaks.
findings.recommendation: Either add an optional gitleaks step to check-local.sh (skipped gracefully if the binary is absent) or document explicitly in the script header that secret scanning is CI-only, so the local-gate contract is honest about what it does and does not cover.

findings.title: Clerk JWT verification never checks the audience (aud) claim
findings.whatExists: verify_clerk_jwt pins algorithm to RS256, verifies issuer, and requires exp/iss/sub via jwt.decode options (backend/auth.py:162-168).
findings.whatsMissing: No audience verification. jwt.decode is called without an `audience=` argument and `aud` is not in the require list. Any RS256 token signed by the same Clerk issuer/JWKS — including tokens minted for a different application, a different API, or a different audience on the same Clerk instance/infra — is accepted as a valid user. There is no CLERK_AUDIENCE / expected-aud env var anywhere (grep for 'aud'/'audience' across backend returns nothing; .env.example has no audience var).
findings.evidence: backend/auth.py:161-169 (jwt.decode with algorithms=["RS256"], issuer=iss, options={"require": ["exp","iss","sub"]} — no audience). Confirmed absent: grep -rn 'audience|\baud\b' backend/*.py backend/tests/*.py returns empty; backend/.env.example:70-76 lists CLERK_JWT_ISSUER/CLERK_JWKS_URL/REQUIRE_CLERK_AUTH but no audience.
findings.recommendation: Add an expected audience (e.g. CLERK_AUDIENCE env or the configured Clerk JWT template aud) and pass audience=... to jwt.decode plus add 'aud' to options['require']. Reject tokens whose aud does not match the API's identifier.

findings.title: X-Forwarded-For rightmost-hop trust has no trusted-proxy allow-list and is bypassable
findings.whatExists: _trusted_forwarded_ip deliberately takes the RIGHTMOST XFF entry to avoid trusting forgeable leftmost client-supplied hops (backend/main.py:126-134), used for both HTTP and WS client-IP derivation (main.py:137-148).
findings.whatsMissing: The rightmost-hop assumption is only valid behind EXACTLY ONE trusted proxy that overwrites/appends XFF. There is no TRUSTED_PROXY / trusted hop-count config and no validation that the request actually arrived via the expected proxy. If the Railway backend is ever reachable directly (public URL) or sits behind a multi-hop edge, an attacker can append their own rightmost XFF value and rotate the rate-limit bucket per request — defeating both HTTP and WS limiters. The comment hardcodes the single-Railway-proxy assumption rather than enforcing it.
findings.evidence: backend/main.py:126-141 (parts[-1] taken unconditionally; comment 'On a single trusted proxy (Railway), the rightmost entry is the real client' — assumption is not enforced anywhere). No trusted-proxy env var in main.py or .env.example.
findings.recommendation: Make the trusted hop count configurable (e.g. TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS) and pick the (N+1)th-from-right entry; or use a vetted library (uvicorn --proxy-headers + forwarded-allow-ips, or starlette ProxyHeadersMiddleware) with an explicit trusted-proxy allow-list. Ensure the backend is not directly reachable bypassing the proxy.

findings.title: Rate limiter is in-process only (resets on restart, ineffective across instances); declared slowapi dependency is unused
findings.whatExists: IPRateLimiter keeps per-IP deques in a process-local dict (backend/main.py:100-119). slowapi>=0.1.9 is declared in requirements.
findings.whatsMissing: State lives only in one process: a restart wipes all buckets, and if Railway runs more than one instance/replica each has its own counters, multiplying the effective limit by the instance count and giving no global guarantee. There is no shared store (Redis) backing the limiter. slowapi is listed in backend/requirements.txt but is imported/used nowhere (grep returns no slowapi usage in backend/*.py), so the dependency is dead and the custom limiter is the only control — self-described as 'demo-stage abuse control' (main.py:101).
findings.evidence: backend/main.py:101-119 (in-memory self._events dict, no external store); backend/requirements.txt:19 lists slowapi but grep -rn 'slowapi' backend/*.py backend/**/*.py returns no usage.
findings.recommendation: For multi-instance production, back rate limiting with a shared store (Redis) or use slowapi with a Redis backend; otherwise document that the backend must run single-instance. Remove the unused slowapi dependency or actually wire it.

findings.title: Unsanitized user free-text is injected directly into LLM prompts (prompt injection)
findings.whatExists: TripRequest validates currency, budget, and trip-date semantics (backend/main.py:241-305); WS rejects oversized/non-JSON messages (main.py:487-495).
findings.whatsMissing: Free-text fields special_requests and stops (and the entire type=chat user message) are interpolated verbatim into LLM system/user prompts with no delimiting, escaping, or instruction-isolation. A user can inject directives like 'ignore previous instructions' into special_requests to steer agent output. Blast radius is limited (output is itinerary/plan text, no privileged tool execution off the injected text, no SSRF), but there is zero prompt-injection defense.
findings.evidence: backend/agents/itinerary.py:91-92 (stops/special read from state) and itinerary.py:116-129 (f-string interpolates `Special requests: {special}` and `Stops / multi-city plan: {stops}` straight into the user prompt). Chat path: backend/main.py:603-624 forwards user_message verbatim into refine_plan.
findings.recommendation: Wrap user free-text in clearly delimited, labeled blocks, instruct the model to treat it as data not instructions, and/or run a lightweight injection filter. Keep treating LLM output as untrusted.

findings.title: Clerk JWT / demo token passed in WebSocket query string and never redacted server-side
findings.whatExists: The frontend reads the WS token from the query string and redacts it in its own debug UI (frontend/prototype.jsx:35). The backend reads token from ?token= / ?demo_token= (backend/auth.py:245-249).
findings.whatsMissing: Bearer credentials in a URL query string are routinely captured in proxy/server access logs, browser history, and APM breadcrumbs. The backend never redacts the WS query: any uvicorn/proxy access log of the WS handshake path, and any Sentry/Starlette breadcrumb that records the request URL, would contain the live Clerk JWT or demo token. There is no scrubbing of token query params in observability (observability.py installs Sentry with default integrations; no before_send scrubber for query strings).
findings.evidence: frontend/prototype.jsx:48-54 (token appended as ?token=/&demo_token= to the WS URL); backend/auth.py:245-249 (reads ws.query_params token); backend/observability.py:54-73 (sentry init with FastApi/Starlette integrations and no before_send/url scrubbing).
findings.recommendation: Prefer sending the token via the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header or a short-lived ticket exchanged over an authenticated HTTP call, rather than the URL. At minimum add a Sentry before_send scrubber that strips token/demo_token query params and ensure access logs do not record the WS query string.

findings.title: All backend dependencies are unpinned (>=) with no Python lockfile — non-reproducible, supply-chain risk
findings.whatExists: backend/requirements.txt lists 19 deps, each with a floor-only specifier (e.g. langgraph>=0.3.0, fastapi>=0.115.0, sqlalchemy>=2.0.30). CI installs with a bare `pip install -r requirements.txt` (ci.yml:77, :136, :188).
findings.whatsMissing: No exact pins (==), no upper bounds, and no lockfile of any kind (no constraints.txt, no pip freeze output, no poetry.lock/Pipfile.lock/uv.lock — verified absent by find). Every fresh install can pull newer minor/major-allowed versions, so CI, local, and deploy can resolve different dependency trees with no record of what was tested. A compromised or breaking upstream release is silently picked up.
findings.evidence: backend/requirements.txt:1-19 (all 19 lines use `>=`); ci.yml:77 `run: pip install -r requirements.txt`; find for constraints*.txt/poetry.lock/Pipfile*/pdm.lock/uv.lock returned zero results.
findings.recommendation: Generate and commit a lockfile: either `pip-compile` (pip-tools) producing a fully-pinned requirements.txt + requirements.in, or `pip freeze > constraints.txt` consumed via `pip install -r requirements.txt -c constraints.txt`, or migrate to uv/poetry. Install in CI with `--require-hashes` for true supply-chain integrity. At minimum pin the direct deps to `==` for the libraries that gate behavior (langgraph, langchain-*, fastapi, sqlalchemy, pydantic).

findings.title: slowapi declared in requirements.txt but never used anywhere in the codebase
findings.whatExists: backend/requirements.txt:19 declares `slowapi>=0.1.9`. The app instead uses a hand-rolled in-process limiter (class IPRateLimiter in backend/main.py:100, instantiated at main.py:122-123 and enforced via _http_rate_limit_dep at main.py:158).
findings.whatsMissing: There is no import or reference to slowapi anywhere in the repo (grep for `slowapi` across all non-venv files returns only the requirements.txt line). The dependency is dead weight — it enlarges the install/attack surface and misleads readers into thinking slowapi is the rate-limiting mechanism.
findings.evidence: backend/requirements.txt:19 `slowapi>=0.1.9`; `grep -rn slowapi` (excluding .venv and requirements.txt) returns empty; backend/main.py:100 `class IPRateLimiter`, main.py:122 `_http_rate_limiter = IPRateLimiter(...)`.
findings.recommendation: Either remove slowapi from requirements.txt (it is unused) or, if a battle-tested limiter is wanted, replace the bespoke IPRateLimiter with slowapi and wire it into FastAPI. Do not ship both an unused dep and a hand-rolled equivalent.

findings.title: starlette and typing_extensions imported by app code but not declared in requirements.txt (rely on transitive resolution)
findings.whatExists: App source imports `starlette` directly (backend/observability.py:9 and backend/security_headers.py:17: `from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware`) and `typing_extensions` directly (backend/state.py:14: `from typing_extensions import NotRequired, TypedDict`). Both currently resolve only because FastAPI/pydantic pull them in transitively.
findings.whatsMissing: Neither starlette nor typing-extensions appears in backend/requirements.txt. Direct first-party imports of a library that is only a transitive dependency is fragile: a future FastAPI release could drop or change its starlette pin, or move typing_extensions to a conditional dependency, silently breaking these imports. Direct deps should be declared directly.
findings.evidence: backend/observability.py:9 and backend/security_headers.py:17 import starlette; backend/state.py:14 imports typing_extensions; neither name appears in backend/requirements.txt:1-19.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit `starlette` and `typing-extensions` entries to requirements.txt (with the same version range FastAPI currently resolves) so the imports are backed by a declared, pinned dependency rather than transitive luck.

findings.title: No pinned Python runtime for deploy — Railway/Nixpacks default drifts from CI 3.12 and local 3.11
findings.whatExists: CI pins Python 3.12 (ci.yml:72, :131, :182). The local venv is 3.11 (.venv/bin/python -> python3.11, per ground truth). scripts/python-bin.sh prefers python3.12 then python3.11 then python3 (python-bin.sh:25). Deploy uses Railway NIXPACKS (railway.json:3-5) and runs `python -m alembic upgrade head && uvicorn` (railway.json:8).
findings.whatsMissing: There is no Python version pin anywhere the deploy build reads: no backend/.python-version, no runtime.txt, no nixpacks.toml, no python version in railway.json (verified absent). Nixpacks will select its own default Python, which can differ from both CI (3.12) and local (3.11). Combined with unpinned deps (deps-config-1), the production interpreter+dependency combination is never the one CI tested. Three different Python versions are in play (3.11 local, 3.12 CI, unknown deploy).
findings.evidence: railway.json:3-8 (NIXPACKS builder, no python version field); ci.yml:72/:131/:182 `python-version: '3.12'`; local venv symlinks to python3.11; find for .python-version/runtime.txt/nixpacks.toml returned no matches.
findings.recommendation: Pin the deploy Python version to match CI: add backend/.python-version (or runtime.txt `python-3.12.x`, or a nixpacks.toml `[phases.setup] nixPkgs = ["python312"]`) and align CI + local venv to the same minor. This guarantees the deployed interpreter equals the tested one.

findings.title: Backend ruff/mypy declared as intended in ci.yml comments but absent — no lint/typecheck gate
findings.whatExists: ci.yml explicitly states the intent to add these: ci.yml:21 'Lint / type-check: new step, same pattern' and ci.yml:88-89 'Future steps go here: mypy, ruff.' alembic.ini even ships commented-out ruff post-write-hook examples (alembic.ini:103-113).
findings.whatsMissing: No ruff config, no mypy config, no flake8/pyproject.toml anywhere in the repo (verified: no pyproject.toml, no ruff/mypy config files exist). The backend has zero static-analysis or type-checking gate; check-local.sh steps 1-4 are doc-sync + compile + unittest + skill tests only (check-local.sh:14-26), with no lint/typecheck. The stated 'future steps' have never materialized.
findings.evidence: ci.yml:88-89 `# Future steps go here: mypy, ruff.`; ci.yml:21; root and backend dir listing show no pyproject.toml / ruff.toml / .ruff.toml / mypy.ini / setup.cfg; check-local.sh:14-26 has no lint/typecheck step.
findings.recommendation: Add a pyproject.toml with [tool.ruff] and [tool.mypy] sections, add `ruff check` and `mypy` deps to a dev-requirements, and wire `ruff check backend` + `mypy backend` as named steps in ci.yml (and into check-local.sh) per the comment's own plan.

findings.title: Frontend has no eslint/prettier/tsconfig — zero static-analysis gate despite ci.yml intent
findings.whatExists: ci.yml:119 declares intent: 'Future steps go here: npm run lint, npm test, bundle-size check.' package.json scripts are only dev/build/preview/e2e (package.json:10-15).
findings.whatsMissing: No lint or typecheck script in package.json, and no eslint config (.eslintrc*/eslint.config.js), no prettier config, no tsconfig.json — confirmed by ground truth and dir listing (codebase is plain JS/JSX, no .ts/.tsx). There is no static-analysis gate on the React 19 frontend at all; only `vite build` + `npm audit` run. A broken-but-bundleable React component, accessibility regression, or unused import is never caught before deploy.
findings.evidence: package.json:10-15 (scripts: dev, build, preview, e2e only); ci.yml:119 future-steps comment; frontend dir listing shows no eslint/prettier/tsconfig files (only package-lock.json among config-like files); ground-truth frontend failure: 'No lint/typecheck script or config exists in the frontend.'
findings.recommendation: Add eslint (with eslint-plugin-react / react-hooks) + prettier configs and a `lint` script to package.json, then add an `npm run lint` step to the frontend CI job and check-local.sh per the ci.yml plan. Consider TypeScript or at least `// @ts-check` + jsconfig for basic type safety.

findings.title: Alembic migrations run in production deploy but are never exercised in CI or the local gate
findings.whatExists: railway.json:8 startCommand runs `python -m alembic upgrade head` on every deploy against Postgres. There is one migration (backend/alembic/versions/36ee394e0625_init_enterprise_floor.py) and alembic.ini + env.py are configured.
findings.whatsMissing: Neither CI (ci.yml) nor scripts/check-local.sh nor scripts/e2e-local.sh ever runs `alembic upgrade head` (grep for alembic/upgrade/migrat across .github/workflows and scripts returns empty). The first time a migration is actually executed is in production at boot. A bad migration (syntax, ordering, Postgres-only DDL that env.py mishandles) only surfaces on Railway, where the healthcheck (railway.json:9, 60s) and restart policy (max 5 retries) would then fail the deploy. Combined with unpinned alembic (requirements.txt:13 `alembic>=1.13`), behavior can change under the feet of an untested path.
findings.evidence: railway.json:8 `python -m alembic upgrade head`; `grep -rn alembic .github/workflows scripts` returns empty; backend/requirements.txt:13 `alembic>=1.13`; only one revision: backend/alembic/versions/36ee394e0625_init_enterprise_floor.py.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI step (and a check-local.sh/e2e step) that spins up a throwaway Postgres (CI services) or SQLite and runs `alembic upgrade head` then `alembic downgrade base`/`alembic check`, so migrations are validated before they hit production deploy.

findings.title: Frontend engines.node range has no upper bound and is not enforced; installed node (v25.9.0) falls outside it
findings.whatExists: package.json:6-9 declares engines.node `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0` and npm `>=11`. CI uses node 22 (ci.yml:102, :141, :191) and installs npm@11 (ci.yml:108). vercel.json builds via `npm ci` (vercel.json:3) with no node version field.
findings.whatsMissing: The engines field is advisory only: there is no engine-strict (no .npmrc with engine-strict=true) and no .nvmrc to pin node for local/Vercel. Ground truth ran on node v25.9.0, which the `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0` range technically excludes intent-wise (it has no upper bound, so 25.x passes >=22.12.0, but no caret-bounded major is declared), yet the build succeeded — proving the constraint is not enforced. Local and Vercel can drift from CI's node 22.
findings.evidence: package.json:6-9 engines; ci.yml:102 `node-version: '22'`; vercel.json:3 buildCommand with no node pin; ground-truth: 'node v25.9.0 ... technically outside the declared range ... engines field is not honored.'
findings.recommendation: Add a .nvmrc (e.g. `22`) and an .npmrc with `engine-strict=true`, and set the Node version in Vercel project settings to match CI's node 22, so the same Node major builds locally, in CI, and on Vercel.

findings.title: Pre-push hook runs the full heavyweight gate; no fast pre-commit stage and no local secret-scan hook
findings.whatExists: Hooks are correctly wired (scripts/install-hooks.sh:6 sets core.hooksPath=.githooks; verified `git config core.hooksPath` = .githooks). .githooks/pre-push (pre-push:6-7) runs check-agent-doc-sync.sh + check-local.sh, which itself does npm ci + full build + 131 unit tests + skill tests (check-local.sh:17-26).
findings.whatsMissing: There is no pre-commit hook (only pre-push exists in .githooks/), so nothing fast (format/lint/quick compile) runs at commit time. There is also no local gitleaks/secret-scan hook even though CI runs gitleaks (ci.yml:47-58) and a .gitleaks.toml exists — secrets are only caught after push reaches CI. The single heavyweight pre-push gate (full npm ci + build) is slow enough that developers may be tempted to `--no-verify`.
findings.evidence: .githooks/ contains only pre-push (dir listing); .githooks/pre-push:6-7 invokes check-local.sh; check-local.sh:18-26 runs npm ci + build + audit; ci.yml:47-58 gitleaks job exists but no corresponding local hook; no pre-commit file present.
findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight pre-commit hook (ruff/eslint --fix + gitleaks protect --staged) for fast feedback and local secret prevention, keeping the full suite at pre-push. Document `--no-verify` discouragement and ensure install-hooks.sh is run as part of onboarding.

findings.title: No database backup / point-in-time-recovery / restore procedure documented anywhere
findings.whatExists: Postgres-backed saved_trips persistence shipped (models.py, repository.py, railway.json runs alembic upgrade head on deploy). User email + saved trip snapshots are stored as durable user data.
findings.whatsMissing: No backup, PITR, snapshot, or restore procedure is documented in deployment-design.md, README, or the runbook (grep for backup/pitr/restore/retention/disaster returns nothing relevant). There is no statement of RPO/RTO, no note on whether Railway Postgres backups are enabled, and no restore-drill step. If the Railway DB is lost or a destructive migration runs, there is no documented path to recover user data.
findings.evidence: grep -rni 'backup|pitr|point-in-time|restore|snapshot|retention|disaster' docs/deployment-design.md README.md returns only unrelated 'state snapshot'/'restored from Postgres' hits (README.md:401,555); no backup section exists. Storage is durable: backend/models.py:74-96 (SavedTrip), backend/repository.py:47-70 (save_trip).
findings.recommendation: Document Railway Postgres backup settings (enable automated backups, state RPO/RTO), add a restore-drill step to the runbook, and pair every destructive migration with a verified backup. Add a periodic backup-verification check.

findings.title: No per-user storage quota — saved_trips inserts are unbounded (cost/abuse + DB bloat)
findings.whatExists: save_trip always INSERTs a new row; list_trips reads back the most recent 50 (limit=50).
findings.whatsMissing: There is no cap on how many trips a single user can save. _handle_save_trip -> _save_trip_sync -> repository.save_trip does an unconditional INSERT every time SAVE is pressed, with no count check, no upsert/replace, and no row cap. An authenticated user (or a script) can insert unlimited rows; list_trips silently hides everything past 50 so the UI even masks the unbounded growth. This is a storage-cost and abuse vector that the rate limiter (per-connection, not per-write) does not cover.
findings.evidence: backend/repository.py:47-70 save_trip = unconditional db.add(SavedTrip(...)); no count/limit. backend/repository.py:73-79 list_trips caps READ at limit=50 but write is uncapped. backend/main.py:752-770 _save_trip_sync has no quota check.
findings.recommendation: Enforce a per-user saved-trips cap (e.g. reject or evict-oldest beyond N), or make SAVE an upsert keyed on (user, gp_slug, dates). Add a unit test for the cap.

findings.title: No Clerk user.deleted webhook — deleting a Clerk account orphans Postgres user_profiles + saved_trips (right-to-erasure / GDPR gap)
findings.whatExists: Auth is pure JWKS JWT verification; user_profiles rows are lazily upserted by clerk_user_id on first persistence op; FK cascade (ondelete=CASCADE) deletes a user's trips when the user_profiles row is deleted.
findings.whatsMissing: There is no Clerk webhook handler (no svix/webhook/user.deleted route anywhere). When a user deletes their account in Clerk, the corresponding user_profiles + saved_trips rows (including their stored email) persist forever in Postgres with no deletion path. There is also no self-service 'delete my account / delete all my data' action in the app (only per-trip delete_trip). For a deployed app storing email + travel data this is a data-retention / right-to-erasure hole.
findings.evidence: grep -rni 'webhook|user.deleted|svix' backend/*.py returns nothing. Only delete_trip exists (backend/repository.py:90-96, backend/main.py:808-811). Email is stored: backend/models.py:57 (UserProfile.email), backend/repository.py:37-38 (set from token).
findings.recommendation: Add a Clerk svix-verified webhook endpoint that deletes the user_profiles row on user.deleted (FK cascade removes trips), or a documented manual erasure procedure, plus optionally a self-serve account/data deletion action.

findings.title: Migrations run inline in the start command — concurrent Railway replicas race on `alembic upgrade head`
findings.whatExists: railway.json startCommand = `cd backend && python -m alembic upgrade head && uvicorn ...`, run on every container start.
findings.whatsMissing: Running migrations as part of each instance's start command is unsafe the moment more than one replica boots (or a deploy overlaps a restart): two processes can call `alembic upgrade head` simultaneously with no advisory lock, racing on DDL. There is no separate release/migrate phase, no migration lock, and no documentation that the service must stay single-replica. Combined with the absence of a Python-version pin and migrations never being exercised in CI (audit deps-config-7), the first concurrent-migration race only surfaces in prod.
findings.evidence: railway.json:8 startCommand couples `alembic upgrade head` to every uvicorn boot; no `--workers` and no replica-count guard documented. No release-phase separation anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Move migrations to a dedicated release/pre-deploy step (or guard with a Postgres advisory lock), and document the single-instance assumption until a release phase exists.

findings.title: WebSocket receive loop has no idle timeout and no cap on concurrent open connections (slow-loris resource exhaustion)
findings.whatExists: There is a per-IP WS *connect-rate* limiter (_ws_connect_limiter.allow), an origin gate, auth-close, a 16KB per-message size cap, and the single event loop offloads DB/plan work to threads.
findings.whatsMissing: The accepted-connection loop is `while True: raw = await ws.receive_text()` with no asyncio.wait_for idle/inactivity timeout, and there is no global cap on the number of simultaneously OPEN WebSocket sessions (the limiter only throttles new-connection rate, not concurrency). An attacker can open many connections that authenticate then go silent; each holds a session dict and a server-side socket indefinitely on the single uvicorn process. This is a classic slow-loris / connection-exhaustion vector against a single-process server.
findings.evidence: backend/main.py:483-484 `while True: raw = await ws.receive_text()` (no wait_for/idle timeout). backend/main.py:377 MAX_WS_MESSAGE_SIZE only bounds message size. _ws_connect_limiter at main.py:466 bounds connect *rate*, not concurrent open count.
findings.recommendation: Wrap receive_text in asyncio.wait_for with an idle timeout that closes stale sockets, and add a global semaphore/counter capping concurrent open WS sessions.

findings.title: Frontend is not responsive/mobile — single fixed maxWidth:680, zero @media queries
findings.whatExists: Desktop layout with a centered column (maxWidth:680, maxHeight:920) and a viewport meta tag.
findings.whatsMissing: There is not a single @media query, matchMedia, or responsive breakpoint anywhere in the frontend (grep across components/, prototype.jsx, src/ returns zero). The app hard-codes a desktop-sized centered card with fixed font sizes (e.g. 9.5px chat text) and a flex column tuned for desktop. On a phone the fixed maxHeight:920 and tiny type produce a degraded, non-adaptive experience. For a trip-planning consumer app, mobile being an afterthought is a real product gap, not just cosmetic.
findings.evidence: grep -rn '@media|max-width|min-width|matchMedia' components/ prototype.jsx src/ returns nothing. Layout root: frontend/prototype.jsx:403 (maxWidth:680, maxHeight:920, fixed). index.html:5 has viewport but no responsive CSS follows.
findings.recommendation: Add responsive breakpoints (or a CSS framework), make the root container fluid on small screens, and add a mobile E2E viewport in Playwright.

findings.title: No SEO / social / PWA metadata — no description, OG/Twitter tags, favicon, robots, or manifest
findings.whatExists: index.html has charset, viewport, and a <title>F1 Paddock Club</title> only.
findings.whatsMissing: index.html has no meta description, no Open Graph / Twitter Card tags (so shared links render with no preview image/text), no favicon (blank browser tab icon), no robots meta, no canonical, no web app manifest, and there is no frontend/public/ directory at all. For a deployed consumer-facing site this hurts shareability and basic polish.
findings.evidence: frontend/index.html:1-16 contains only charset/viewport/title; grep for 'favicon|og:|twitter:|description|robots|manifest' in index.html returns nothing. `ls frontend/public` does not exist (no static assets dir).
findings.recommendation: Add favicon, meta description, OG/Twitter tags with a preview image, robots/canonical, and (optionally) a manifest; create frontend/public for static assets.

findings.title: Sentry is initialized on the frontend but never consumed (no ErrorBoundary, no captureException, no PII scrubbing)
findings.whatExists: src/main.jsx calls Sentry.init when VITE_SENTRY_DSN_FRONTEND is set, with tracesSampleRate 0.1.
findings.whatsMissing: Beyond the single init call, Sentry is never used: no Sentry.ErrorBoundary, no Sentry.captureException, and no beforeSend/denyUrls scrubber. (The audit noted the missing React error boundary, but missed that the Sentry init itself is functionally inert AND unscrubbed.) Crucially the WS auth token is carried in the URL query string (buildWsUrl appends ?token=JWT); the frontend redactToken regex only sanitizes debug-log STRINGS, not what Sentry breadcrumbs / browser history actually capture, so a live Clerk JWT can land in Sentry. Default Sentry config also sends request URLs/PII. No replay, no release tagging, no user context either.
findings.evidence: src/main.jsx:12 is the ONLY Sentry usage (grep 'Sentry.' across components/prototype/src returns only the init). Token-in-URL: frontend/prototype.jsx:47-53 buildWsUrl appends `?token=`/`?demo_token=`. redactToken only operates on log strings: frontend/prototype.jsx:35. No beforeSend scrubber anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the app in Sentry.ErrorBoundary, add a beforeSend that strips token/demo_token query params and disables sending request URLs, and set release/environment tagging. Consider moving the WS token to a subprotocol/header rather than the URL.

findings.title: No uptime/alerting on health probes or errors — observability is collect-only with no routing
findings.whatExists: /healthz + /readyz endpoints, RequestIdMiddleware, JSON logging, optional Sentry, and a manual deploy-smoke workflow.
findings.whatsMissing: There is no automated monitoring or alerting layer: nothing polls /readyz on a schedule, no uptime monitor (Better Uptime/Pingdom/etc.) or Railway alert is documented, no Sentry alert rule, and deploy-smoke is workflow_dispatch-only (the audit noted deploy-smoke is manual but framed it as a smoke gap, not an ongoing-monitoring gap). So a post-deploy DB outage that flips /readyz to 503, or a Sentry error spike, notifies no one. Observability is purely collection with no signal routing.
findings.evidence: health.py:29-40 /readyz returns 503 on DB down but nothing consumes it on a schedule. .github/workflows/deploy-smoke.yml on: workflow_dispatch only (manual). observability.py:54-73 init_sentry has no alerting config. No cron/scheduled workflow exists (.github/workflows has only ci.yml + deploy-smoke.yml).
findings.recommendation: Add a scheduled uptime check against /readyz (cron workflow or external monitor) with alert routing, and configure Sentry alert rules for error-rate spikes.

findings.title: No LICENSE file — legal blocker for a public repo with a public deploy
findings.whatExists: Public-style repo with README, CHANGELOG, contributor-oriented AGENTS/CLAUDE docs, and a public Vercel/Railway deploy story.
findings.whatsMissing: There is no LICENSE / LICENSE.md / COPYING file anywhere. Without a license, default copyright applies and no one may legally reuse, fork, or contribute to the code, and dependency/SBOM tooling cannot classify it. For a project framed as a portfolio/enterprise-floor deploy this is a concrete legal omission the audit's docs-consistency dimension did not flag.
findings.evidence: `ls LICENSE LICENSE.md COPYING` -> none found at repo root.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit LICENSE (e.g. MIT/Apache-2.0) appropriate to the intended use.

findings.title: No Dependabot/Renovate — unpinned deps never even receive update PRs, so the unpinned-deps risk is never serviced
findings.whatExists: CI runs gitleaks and `npm audit --audit-level=moderate`; backend deps use >= ranges (audit deps-config-1).
findings.whatsMissing: There is no .github/dependabot.yml, renovate.json, or .renovaterc. The audit flagged that deps are unpinned and there is no lockfile for Python, but it missed that there is also no automated dependency-update mechanism at all — so neither the unpinned ranges nor the npm lockfile get serviced by update PRs or security alerts. npm audit only reports at build time; it does not open fix PRs, and there is nothing equivalent for Python deps.
findings.evidence: `ls .github/dependabot.yml renovate.json .renovaterc` -> NONE. .github/workflows contains only ci.yml + deploy-smoke.yml (no scheduled dependency job).
findings.recommendation: Add a Dependabot/Renovate config for both pip (backend/requirements.txt) and npm (frontend) plus GitHub Actions, alongside pinning deps.

findings.title: E2E and runtime depend on a drifting GP calendar / hardcoded near-term dates — tests silently rot as races pass
findings.whatExists: Smoke specs were migrated Canadian GP -> Italian GP specifically because of calendar drift (harness STATE.md note), and the smoke spec fills explicit travel dates 2026-05-22/2026-05-26.
findings.whatsMissing: The deterministic E2E lane is time-coupled to a live, advancing calendar: the harness itself records migrating specs off the Canadian GP because 'today past 2026-05-24 race date', and smoke.spec.js hardcodes depart 2026-05-22 / return 2026-05-26 — both already in the PAST as of the current date (2026-06-02). As more 2026 races pass, the chosen GP and these literal dates will keep falling out of the calendar window, making the 'deterministic' lane non-deterministic over time and forcing recurring manual spec edits. There is no relative-date strategy (e.g. compute a future date) and no test that the calendar/date layer degrades sanely once all listed races are past.
findings.evidence: .harness/STATE.md:56 documents the Canadian->Italian migration 'for calendar drift (today past 2026-05-24 race date)'. frontend/e2e/smoke.spec.js:47-52 hardcodes 2026-05-22/2026-05-26 (past relative to 2026-06-02). frontend/domain/tripDates.js has no today-relative validation (no Date.now/past check).
findings.recommendation: Make E2E dates relative to a fixed/mocked clock or compute future dates, and add coverage for the all-races-past degradation path so the lane stays deterministic.

findings.title: Harness 'done' status contradicts shipped-deploy claims — deploy presented as DONE while the gate (T-001) is still awaiting a verdict
findings.whatExists: README Roadmap + CHANGELOG [Unreleased] + railway.json + vercel.json present the enterprise-floor deploy config as shipped/done. Harness STATE.md still lists Phase 4 'deploy readiness' with T-001 awaiting reviewer R10 verdict and T-DEPLOY-VERIFY unstarted.
findings.whatsMissing: The audit flagged many docs-vs-reality staleness issues (current.md, ZH README, README status table) but missed this specific live contradiction in the project's own control plane: the harness — the source of truth agents are told to follow — says the deploy-verification work (T-DEPLOY-VERIFY) is planned-but-unstarted and is gated on T-001, which is itself only 'awaiting verdict', yet the user-facing docs already declare the deploy 'done'. An agent following the harness would conclude deploy verification is incomplete; a reader following README would conclude it is finished. This is an unresolved status mismatch about whether the deploy is actually gate-verified.
findings.evidence: .harness/STATE.md:4 'Phase: 4 (hardening / E2E automation / deploy readiness)', :8 T-001 'awaiting reviewer R10 verdict', :9-10 'Planned next: T-DEPLOY-VERIFY ... still gated on T-001 close'. Contrast: railway.json/vercel.json committed + README Roadmap '4.7 enterprise floor ... (done)' (per audit docs-consistency findings).
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the harness and docs: either close T-001/T-DEPLOY-VERIFY and update STATE.md, or downgrade the README 'done' claim to 'config shipped, verification pending' until the gate closes.

findings.title: No product analytics / usage telemetry — no insight into funnel, plan success rate, or feature adoption
findings.whatExists: Sentry error/trace SDK is wired (frontend init + optional backend), and there is a debug trace overlay (?debug).
findings.whatsMissing: There is no product-analytics instrumentation of any kind (grep for analytics/gtag/posthog/mixpanel/plausible returns nothing). Nothing records funnel steps (calendar view -> GP select -> plan run -> save), plan success/failure rates, refine usage, or save/load adoption. Sentry traces capture errors/performance, not product usage. For a deployed product there is no signal to know whether features work for users or where they drop off.
findings.evidence: grep -rni 'analytics|gtag|posthog|mixpanel|plausible' frontend (components/prototype/src) returns nothing. Only Sentry (error/trace) is present (src/main.jsx:12).
findings.recommendation: Add lightweight, consent-aware product analytics for the core funnel and feature usage, and document the data collected in a privacy note.

findings.title: No LLM cost/spend guard or per-call-type budget — refine + multi-agent fan-out can run up unbounded provider cost
findings.whatExists: .env.example documents free-tier provider limits and a default cheap model (gpt-4o-mini); get_llm sets max_tokens per call; MAX_CONCURRENT_PLANS bounds concurrent plan runs.
findings.whatsMissing: There is no spend/quota guard on LLM usage: no per-user request quota, no daily token/cost ceiling, no circuit breaker on provider spend, and (per audit) no per-call timeout/retry. MAX_CONCURRENT_PLANS bounds concurrency but not total volume — an authenticated user can repeatedly trigger plan + refine (multi-agent fan-out, each calling the provider) with no cost ceiling. For a deploy with a real OPENAI_API_KEY this is an open-ended billing exposure. The rate limiter is per-IP connect-rate, not per-identity LLM-call budget.
findings.evidence: backend/llm.py only sets model/temperature/max_tokens (lines 80-89, 105-114) — no cost tracking. No per-user LLM quota anywhere (grep for quota returns nothing in app code). Rate limit is per-IP connect (main.py:466), unrelated to LLM spend.
findings.recommendation: Add a per-identity LLM-call/token budget (daily ceiling + 429 on exceed) and a provider-spend circuit breaker; surface usage in logs/metrics.

findings.title: deploy-smoke bundle scan is brittle and easily silently-skipped (false-green secret check)
findings.whatExists: deploy-smoke greps the built JS bundle for a fixed list of forbidden secret substrings (CLERK_SECRET_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, etc.).
findings.whatsMissing: The bundle secret-scan can silently pass without scanning anything: if the regex `/assets/index-[hash].js` does not match the index HTML (e.g. Vite output naming changes, code-splitting, or a CDN-rewritten path), the step prints 'Could not locate built JS asset; skipping bundle scan' and EXITS 0 — a false green on a security-relevant check. It also only matches literal env-var NAMES, not actual secret VALUE shapes (sk-..., a real DSN), so a leaked value not adjacent to its variable name would pass. Being manual-only (workflow_dispatch) compounds this. The audit covered deploy-smoke being manual but not that its core secret check is fail-open.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-smoke.yml: the bundle step echoes 'Could not locate built JS asset; skipping bundle scan' and does not fail when the script tag is not found; forbidden list is variable-name substrings only, not value patterns.
findings.recommendation: Make a missing/unscannable asset a hard failure, scan all emitted JS assets (not just the first), and add value-shape patterns (sk-, DSN regex) in addition to variable names.
